title: Mayer-Vietoris sequences are compatible with pullback
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $X=U\cup V$ a union of two open subschemes, and $U'=g^{-1}(U)$, $V'=g^{-1}(V)$, so $Y=U'\cup V'$ and $U'\cap V'=g^{-1}(U\cap V)$; for $W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}$ write $W'=g^{-1}(W)$ and $g_W:W'\to W$ for the restriction of $g$. Let $\mathcal G$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then the pullback maps of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], $g^*:H^q(X_{\Et},\mathcal G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},g^{-1}\mathcal G)$ and $g_W^*:H^q(W_{\Et},\mathcal G|_W)\to H^q(W'_{\Et},g_W^{-1}(\mathcal G|_W))\cong H^q(W'_{\Et},(g^{-1}\mathcal G)|_{W'})$ (the identification being $H^q$ of the isomorphism $g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}\cong j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], both sides being inverse images along $g\circ j_{W'}=j_W\circ g_W$), form a morphism from the Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] for $(X,U,V,\mathcal G)$ to the one for $(Y,U',V',g^{-1}\mathcal G)$: every square, including those with the connecting maps $\delta$, commutes.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50 (lemma-mayer-vietoris) and its proof (the short exact sequences $0\to\mathcal I^\bullet(X)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U)\oplus\mathcal I^\bullet(V)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V)\to0$ of an injective resolution); the compatibility with pullback is not stated in the source (agent-identified gap: it is needed for the reduction of Theorem 09YQ to the affine case)

proof.text: Use the connecting-pullback construction to choose delta_X and delta_Y, both exact sequences and their connecting square.

Choose the eleven existential restriction and pullback maps to be their prescribed cohomologyMap/composition formulas. All eleven identification assertions are reflexive; the sequence exactness assertions are the supplied ones.
Apply whole-scheme restriction naturality separately to U and V. This proves the first kind of square in every degree.
Apply nested-open restriction naturality to U∩V≤U and to U∩V≤V. Subtract their equalities; additivity of the restricted pullback map gives the difference square.
Assemble the eleven map identifications, the two exact sequences and the three kinds of squares with the chosen connecting maps. The statement is unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A50 construction and pullback functoriality; Lean reduction by D2: ordinary squares proved from composition coherence, exactness and connecting square isolated as a strict part of the argument.

Proof written by the agent (Stacks states neither this compatibility nor anything close; Tag 0A50's construction is used) in five steps along the brief's plan: (1) injective resolutions I on X and J on Y with augmentation s', and beta: g^{-1}I -> J with beta g^{-1}(s) = s' exactly (lift via lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived; a homotopy out of a complex concentrated in degree 0 into one vanishing in degree -1 is zero), so that by clause 2 of lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial g^* = H^q(a |-> beta(eta_g(a))) on I(X) -> J(Y), the definition def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback being 'unit, then the comparison map to the resolution'; (2) the maps phi_W = beta(W') o eta_g(W): I(W) -> J(W') form a morphism of the short exact sequences of sections (same sign convention), by naturality of the unit and beta; (3) lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality; (4) H^q(phi_W) = H^q(kappa_G) o g_W^* under the identifications rho of the Mayer-Vietoris node: clause 2 again for g_W with M = j_{W'}^{-1}J and beta_W = j_{W'}^{-1}(beta) o kappa_I, H^q(kappa_G) lifted by the identity, and the compatibility of the units with the restriction isomorphisms, which is a new agent-identified node lem-weil-pbc-open-restriction-pullback-unit (unsplit); (5) assembly. The construction of the Mayer-Vietoris sequence (short exact sequence of sections of an injective resolution, rho-identifications, independence of the resolution) is only in the proof of lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris, not in its statement; the steps cite it with the proof steps named.
